title: Kernel and cone inversion for a thick Verdier quotient
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], and let $\mathcal S$ be a strictly full triangulated subcategory closed under retracts (if an object of $\mathcal D$ is a direct summand of an object of $\mathcal S$, it belongs to $\mathcal S$). The Verdier quotient $Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/\mathcal S$ is an exact functor, obtained by inverting every morphism which occurs as the first map of a distinguished triangle whose third object belongs to $\mathcal S$. For every object $A$, $Q(A)$ is a zero object if and only if $A\in\mathcal S$.

source.place: Tags 05RG, 05RI and 05RK; labels lemma-construct-multiplicative-system, definition-quotient-category, lemma-kernel-quotient

proof.text: Put $W=\{f:X\to Y\mid X\xrightarrow fY\to C\to X[1]\text{ is distinguished for some }C\in\mathcal S\}$. Membership in the strictly full triangulated subcategory $\mathcal S$ contains zero, is invariant under all integer shifts and isomorphisms, and has the two-out-of-three property on distinguished triangles. Apply [lem-trf-triangulated-subcategory-cone-system] to this subcategory: $W$ contains identities, is closed under composition, has left and right calculi of fractions and is compatible with the triangulated structure. Define $\mathcal D/\mathcal S=W^{-1}\mathcal D$ and its functor $Q$ by localization as in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]; no saturation assumption is needed for this part of that definition. Thus $Q$ inverts exactly the specified class in the sense of being localization at that class (this does not assert that no other morphisms become invertible).

source.place: Tag 05RG, lemma-construct-multiplicative-system, first assertion; Tag 05RI, definition-quotient-category

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-localization-triangles-05r6] to $W$ and the triangulated category $\mathcal D$. Its hypotheses are supplied by Step 1, without needing saturation: the localization inherits a triangulated structure and $Q$ is exact. In particular, by the definition of an exact functor [def-weil-triangulated-category], $Q$ is additive and therefore sends every zero morphism to a zero morphism.

Let $A\in\mathcal S$. By inverse rotation of the contractible distinguished triangle $A\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}A\to0\to A[1]$, the triangle $0\to A\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}A\to0$ is distinguished, up to the canonical shift-of-zero isomorphism. Hence $0:0\to A$ belongs to $W$. The morphism $Q(0):Q(0)\to Q(A)$ is both invertible (localization) and zero (Step 2). Composing this zero morphism with its inverse gives $\mathrm{id}_{Q(A)}=0$. Every map to or from $Q(A)$ is then zero, by composing with this identity; the zero maps exist, so $Q(A)$ is both initial and terminal.

source.place: Tag 05RI and Tag 05RK, lemma-kernel-quotient, forward containment, expanded using TR1 and TR2

proof.text: Conversely suppose $Q(A)$ is a zero object. Then $Q(\mathrm{id}_A)=\mathrm{id}_{Q(A)}=0=Q(0_{A,A})$. Apply [lem-pc-right-fraction-common-refinement] with $M=N=P_1=P_2=A$, $s_1=s_2=\mathrm{id}_A\in W$, $f_1=\mathrm{id}_A$ and $f_2=0_{A,A}$. The right calculus required there is Step 1. The resulting maps $a_1,a_2:R\to A$ satisfy $a_1=a_2=s\in W$ and $a_1=0\circ a_2=0$. Consequently $s=0:R\to A$ is a member of $W$. This is a direct application of equality of fractions, not an assumption that $W$ is saturated.

source.place: Tag 04VJ, lemma-equality-morphisms-right-localization, and the preceding right-fraction equivalence relation; cf. derived.tex, lemma-kernel-localization

proof.text: By the definition of $W$, choose a distinguished triangle $R\xrightarrow{0}A\xrightarrow gC\xrightarrow hR[1]$ with $C\in\mathcal S$. Apply clause (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] with its $X=R$, $Y=A$, $Z=C$, $u=0$, $W=R[1]$ and $c=\mathrm{id}_{R[1]}$; its hypothesis $u[1]\circ c=0$ holds since the shift is additive. It gives $k:R[1]\to C$ with $h\circ k=\mathrm{id}_{R[1]}$. We show that $(g,k):A\oplus R[1]\to C$ is an isomorphism. By TR2 [def-weil-triangulated-category] the rotation $A\xrightarrow gC\xrightarrow hR[1]\xrightarrow{-0[1]=0}A[1]$ is distinguished. Put $p=\mathrm{id}_C-k\circ h$. Then $h\circ p=h-h\circ k\circ h=0$, so clause (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] for the rotated triangle, with its $W=C$, gives $q:C\to A$ with $p=g\circ q$. Clause (ii) for the original triangle shows that $g\circ a=0$ forces $a=0\circ b=0$, for every $a:V\to A$. By clause (i), $h\circ g=0$, so $p\circ g=g$ and $g\circ(q\circ g-\mathrm{id}_A)=0$; also $g\circ q\circ k=p\circ k=k-k\circ h\circ k=0$. Hence $q\circ g=\mathrm{id}_A$ and $q\circ k=0$. With $h\circ g=0$ and $h\circ k=\mathrm{id}_{R[1]}$ this says that $(q,h):C\to A\oplus R[1]$ is a left inverse of $(g,k)$, and $g\circ q+k\circ h=p+k\circ h=\mathrm{id}_C$ says that it is a right inverse. Thus $A$ is a direct summand of $C\in\mathcal S$, and the closure of $\mathcal S$ under direct summands gives $A\in\mathcal S$. Together with Step 3 this is the claimed equivalence.
